correctness.rationale: Explicit absent-species indicator expansion yields the exact covariance identity; complete enumeration of integer abundance partitions for N=2..9 (590 profile-depth cases) independently reproduces exact rational signs via labeled-subset enumeration. At N=10, two exact positive cases (4,1^6) and (5,1^5) occur at depth two. Symbolic factorization for (t,1^s) at m=2 and exactly -ts/(t+s)^2 at m=N-1 proves every asserted unbounded family; finite tests do not substitute for these general identities. Boundaries m<N and normalization checked.

value.rationale: The sharp ten-individual threshold identifies the minimum finite ecological community where a high observed species count predicts increased immediate discovery, contradicting naive richness-depletion intuition. The closed abundance-family formula proves an opposite sign near census at arbitrarily large population sizes, thus separating shallow and deep sampling regimes. This is a motivated discrete dependence boundary for sequential biodiversity estimation rather than an arbitrary numerical statistic. The model is restricted to perfectly identified uniform finite sampling.
